items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: as he once said, Willie Loman had tough territory.

ctx.x: Nat, could you do us a favor? The people listening to this interview long after we’re all gone will be longing for some information. You mentioned your book Boston Boy. I hope anyone who’s ever taken the time to listen to this interview will read that as a preface, but it’s so good to hear it from your mouth. Could you paint – could you introduce your parents to us briefly. Give us a little character sketch, if we had met them.

My mother had been a very independent woman, growing up in Orthodox Jewish religion. For example, when her father died, she insisted on saying the prayer for the dead and speaking at the shul, the synagogue. That was rarely done. When she was at Filene’s, she became, I think, a head cashier. Then after her marriage, she was pretty much a housewife. My father was a role model to me in a number of ways. I’ll give you a quick example. When I was a kid he took me to a restaurant and forgot to pay the check. After…
Nat, were your grandparents a part of the equation, part of the picture.
